newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends off contract lows, but seen weak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends off contract lows, but seen weak.

text.p: London cocoa values trimmed early losses on Monday but were unable to shrug off a stubborn downtrend that has dragged the market to contract lows.
Producers were not offering cocoa, enabling prices to receive some support at the lows. But the market also lacked strength to break to higher ground amid thin industry demand.
"Cocoa is readily available to them so they won't buy until they feel the shortage," said one trader.

Early attempts to chase sell stops led the benchmark March position to its life-low low of 865 stg for the second time. It recovered slightly and stayed almost static in afternoon exchanges, ending the day at 876 stg a tonne, down three.
Traders said lack of follow-through selling in New York after Friday's nine-month lows lent support to London.
But the market was unmoved by the latest weekly Ghana cocoa purchases which seemed to confirm views that the West African harvest is likely to lag behind last year.

"People are fairly convinced that the arrivals we've seen so far are disappointing," said the trader. "But we are only three months into the season...we've still got the rest of the season for what could be heavy arrivals."

Purchases in the 10th and the 9th week of 1996/97 ending December 19 and December 12 were 11,795 and 10,969 tonnes compared with 15,973 in December 21 and 16,254 in December 14 corresponding to the 11th and the 10th week of 1995/96.

Cumulative purchases stood sharply lower than the same period of last season. By the end of December 19, 1996 they totalled 184,034 tonnes compared with 259,718 by December 21, 1995, the Ghana Cocoa Board said on Monday.
While the data signalled a smaller West African main harvest this year, the Ivorian mid crop could still provide a quick recovery if it came in as large as last year, analysts said.
"The big question is the size of the mid crop," said one.
Monday's total volume of 2,809 lots included arbitrage deals against New York with nearbys bid against New York. On switches, the March/May spread traded into 19 stg.
Technically the market is looking weak with March still likely to break 865 stg and drift towards the 17-month low of 847 on second-month continuation to test support, analysts said.
